lectures.title: What is an AVL Tree? Why do we need it?

cues.en: All right.
In this section we are going to learn about AVL tree.
Now what is AVL tree.
AVL tree is a self-balancing binary search tree where a difference between the heads of left and right
subtrees cannot be more than one for all nodes.
Now from this definition, you can easily see that an AVL tree is also a type of binary search tree.
This means that all properties of binary tree are applicable for AVL trees also.
So let's say we have a binary search tree like this.
So we can easily see that on the left subtree we have the nodes which are less than the root node.
And on the right subtree we have the nodes which are greater than the root node.
So this is applicable for all nodes over here.
Now the question is how can we identify that if this binary search tree is a AVL tree or not.
Because in AVL tree we have said that we have an additional property where it says that the difference
between the heads of left and right subtrees cannot be more than one.
So this is going to be applicable for all nodes.
Now to be able to check for this tree First we are going to start from the root node.
Now after selecting the root node we need to find out the left subtree's height.
So in this case the left subtree is this one.
The height of this left subtree is three and we need to find the height of the right subtree.
So for this right subtree, the height is two and the difference between them is one.
So in the definition it says that it cannot be more than one.
So this is fine for us because it's equal to one.
Now after checking this we cannot say that this is an AVL tree because we have to check it for all nodes.
So we are going to continue to the left subtree.
So here the root node is 50.
The left subtree height is two and the right subtree height is one.
So the difference is one.
So this also confirms with the AVL tree property.
So that's why we are going to continue to the next subtree.
So in this case this is going to be the next subtree.
So we can easily see that the left subtree height is one and the right subtree height is one.
So the difference between them is going to be zero.
So this is fine also.
So we are going to continue to the right subtree.
So in the right subtree also the left subtree height is one and the right subtree height is one.
So the difference between them is zero.
So we can say that this whole tree over here is an AVL tree.
So as you can see we have checked this property for all nodes over here.
So after making sure that all nodes conforms with the AVL tree property we can say that this tree is
an AVL tree.
Now let's say the tree is like this.
So we have removed this right child from here.
So in this case also we are going to start from the root node.
So in the root node we know that the left subtree height is three and the right subtree height is two.
So we don't have any problem over here.
Now if we continue to the left subtree.
So here we see that we don't have any right subtree.
But the left subtree height is two and the right subtree height is zero.
So the difference between them is two.
So we can easily see that this is not applicable.
And we cannot call this tree an AVL tree.
So the rebalancing needs over here to make this binary search tree as an AVL tree.
So another example can be like this.
Now here again if you start from the root node the left subtree height is four and the right subtree
height is two.
So we can easily see that this binary search tree is not an AVL tree.
So rebalancing needs over here to make this binary search tree as an AVL tree.
So in our upcoming lectures you will see that by doing rotations over here we can make a binary search
tree to the AVL tree.
Now the question is why do we need AVL tree.
So let's say we have a binary search tree like this.
First we have inserted ten 1020 then 30 then 40.
So every time it's bigger than the previous one.
That's why it's inserted as a right child.
Now if we search for for example, 40, the time complexity for this search is going to be o n because
we have to loop through all the nodes to find out the 40 over here.
Now in case of AVL tree it's going to be different.
So if we do some rotation over here and make it as an AVL tree like this.
So if we search for 40 in this case the time complexity is going to be all again because this is going
to be balanced binary search tree.
And in balanced binary search tree we know that for searching any given element is going to be all again
which is faster than on time complexity.
So hopefully with this lecture you have understood what is AVL tree and why do we need it.
